pr.title: feat(app): `basePath` option for the constructor, deprecate `app.basePath()`

summary: The PR adds a `basePath` option to the Hono constructor, refactors `_basePath` to a private class field (`#basePath`), and deprecates `app.basePath()`. It also simplifies `route()` to no longer route through the deprecated `basePath()` method, instead cloning and setting `#basePath` directly, and removes the one-argument `route(path)` overload (which was already deprecated for removal in v4). Tests were updated/added to cover the new option alongside existing deprecated usage, but the removal of the distinct one-argument `route()` overload changes its inferred return type at the type level.

findings.rationale: The one-argument `route<SubPath extends string>(path: SubPath)` overload (typed to return Hono<E, RemoveBlankRecord<S>, BasePath>) was removed from the type signatures, leaving only the two-argument overload with an optional `app` param. Any caller relying on the removed overload's distinct return type (RemoveBlankRecord<S>) for one-arg route() calls will now get the merged-schema type instead, which is a type-level behavior change though the JS-level call still works via the optional second param.
findings.suggestedCheck: Search for any external consumers or internal usages of `app.route('/x')` (single-arg) and confirm TypeScript type inference is still acceptable; check hono.test.ts type-level assertions for route() with a single argument.
